_readme: Single editable content record for the site. Every fact carries a `status`. confirmed = approved by Dr. Abela or office staff (only these appear in a production build). public = corroborated in public sources, awaiting practice confirmation (shown in staging builds with a marker). draft = copy written for the site, awaiting Dr. Abela's approval (shown in staging with a Draft marker). lead = secondary source only (never rendered; listed in the content-gaps report). missing = not yet supplied (staging shows a placeholder; production omits). `source` cites the research handoff reference numbers.

shortBio.value: Oliver G. Abela, MD, FACC, is a Tampa cardiologist with fellowship training in cardiovascular disease, interventional cardiology, and advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology. His background includes complex coronary intervention, structural heart procedures, and cardiovascular imaging. He earned his medical degree at Michigan State University and completed postgraduate training in Michigan, Ohio, Nevada, and Arizona.

areasOfCare.title: Coronary artery disease
areasOfCare.summary: Chest pain, shortness of breath with exertion, prior heart attack, and blocked or narrowed heart arteries.
areasOfCare.detail: Care starts with evaluation and a treatment plan, which may include medications, risk-factor management, and testing. When a blockage needs treatment, Dr. Abela's training includes coronary stenting (PCI), complex and high-risk PCI, and chronic total occlusion (CTO) procedures.
areasOfCare.settingNote: Catheter-based procedures are done in a hospital catheterization lab, not in the office.

areasOfCare.title: Advanced heart failure
areasOfCare.summary: Weakened or stiff heart muscle, fluid buildup, and heart failure that is difficult to control.
areasOfCare.detail: Dr. Abela completed a fellowship in advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology. Treatment adjusts medications, tracks symptoms and fluid, and brings in hospital care when it is needed.
areasOfCare.settingNote: Which monitoring services are available through the office has not been confirmed.

areasOfCare.title: Structural heart and valve disease
areasOfCare.summary: Narrowed or leaking heart valves, holes in the heart (ASD/PFO), and stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.
areasOfCare.detail: His procedural training covers transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), transcatheter mitral repair (MitraClip), ASD/PFO closure, and left atrial appendage closure (Watchman). An office visit comes first to decide whether a procedure is right for you.
areasOfCare.settingNote: These procedures are performed in the hospital.

areasOfCare.title: Cardiac imaging
areasOfCare.summary: Echocardiography (heart ultrasound) and cardiac CT to look at the heart's structure and function.
areasOfCare.detail: Dr. Abela holds credentials in echocardiography and cardiovascular CT. Imaging results guide diagnosis and the planning of any procedure.
areasOfCare.settingNote: Whether testing is done in the office or at an outside facility has not been confirmed.

areasOfCare.title: Prevention and cholesterol management
areasOfCare.summary: High cholesterol, family history of heart disease, and lowering future cardiovascular risk.
areasOfCare.detail: Dr. Abela holds a clinical lipidology credential and has published research on how arterial plaque ruptures. Visits cover cholesterol treatment and other risk factors.

areasOfCare.title: Cardiogenic shock and circulatory support
areasOfCare.summary: Critical heart failure that needs temporary mechanical support of the circulation.
areasOfCare.detail: Hospital care for patients whose heart cannot pump enough blood on its own, including Impella heart-pump support during high-risk procedures.

areasOfCare.title: Pulmonary embolism intervention
areasOfCare.summary: Catheter-based removal of blood clots in the lungs.
areasOfCare.detail: Listed as a clinical interest (mechanical thrombectomy).
areasOfCare.note: Confirm this is still part of his current clinical work.

trials.summary: A clinical trial evaluating an investigational device, the Aortix system, for patients hospitalized with acute heart failure. The device is investigational. It is not an approved routine treatment.

visitSteps.title: Your first visit

visitSteps.title: A clear plan
visitSteps.text: You leave knowing the next steps, whether that is testing, treatment, or planning for a procedure.

faq.a: Yes, call 911 if you have chest pain, severe shortness of breath, fainting, or other symptoms that could be a heart attack or stroke. The office and this website are not for emergencies.

faq.q: Are heart procedures done in the office?
faq.a: No. Catheter-based procedures such as stents, and structural heart procedures such as TAVR, are performed in a hospital. Office visits are for evaluation, planning, and follow-up.

faq.q: What should I bring to my first visit?
faq.a: Your ID and insurance card, a list of your medications, and any recent test results or hospital records. The Patient Information page has the full list.

whyChoose.title: One specialist across the whole path
whyChoose.text: Fellowship training in cardiovascular disease, interventional cardiology, and advanced heart failure, plus credentials in echocardiography and cardiac CT. Diagnosis, imaging, procedures, and long-term care sit with one physician.

whyChoose.title: Procedures when they are needed
whyChoose.text: Training in complex coronary stenting, chronic total occlusion, TAVR, MitraClip, and Watchman. Procedures are performed in the hospital and followed up in the office.

whyChoose.title: Care informed by research
whyChoose.text: Principal investigator for a heart failure clinical trial and a published author on coronary plaque and structural heart cases.
